chunks: And Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man and a woman who both perish, and the heirs of the woman come and claim the dowry (sadaq) from the heirs of the man. He said: 'And they have perished and the inheritance has been divided?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'They have nothing.' I said: 'And if the woman was alive and came after the death of her husband claiming her dowry?' He said: 'She has nothing, and she had remained with him acknowledging [the debt] until her husband perished.' I said: 'And if she died while he was alive, and her heirs came claiming her dowry from him?' He said: 'And she had remained [alive] until she died not claiming it?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'She has nothing.' I said: 'And if he divorced her and she came claiming her dowry?' He said: 'And she had remained not claiming it until he divorced her?' He said: 'She has nothing.' I said: 'When is the limit of that, i.e., if I claim it, it will not be for her?' He said: 'When she was presented to him and entered his house, and then claimed it after that, she has nothing. Indeed, it is much for her that an oath be sworn by Allah that she has no dowry from him. [Whether] little or much.'

key_terms.الصَّدَاق: Dowry (sadaq), specifically the portion of the mahr paid or due at the time of divorce or death.
key_terms.يَهْلِكَانِ جَمِيعًا: Both perish/die simultaneously, a scenario for simultaneous death inheritance rules.
key_terms.يُسْتَحْلَفَ: To be made to swear an oath (oath of claim/debt clearance).

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on claiming a wife's dowry from her husband's heirs if she died without formally claiming it during his lifetime?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the failure to actively claim the dowry (mahr) during the husband's lifetime results in its forfeiture, as the husband's oath suffices to discharge the debt. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that silence or inaction in claiming a known debt can be interpreted as a waiver, distinguishing it from cases where the debt is explicitly acknowledged. The text further specifies that once the wife enters the husband's home and remains silent, the burden of proof shifts, and a simple oath by the husband clears the liability regardless of the amount.
